questions.q: What would one day without your main site cost, and has anyone put a number on it?
questions.why: Turns recovery objectives into a business decision.
questions.need: The cost of a day without the main site is known and agreed
questions.how: Put a number on it with finance and the business owner

questions.q: When was the last full recovery test, and what went wrong in it?
questions.why: Tests always find something; no test means it is still hidden.
questions.need: A full recovery test runs regularly, and its findings are closed
questions.how: Schedule a non-disruptive test failover and track what it finds

questions.q: Which sites and branches have no copy of their workloads anywhere?
questions.why: Unprotected sites are the first gap to close.
questions.need: Every site and branch has a copy of its workloads
questions.how: Connect the unprotected sites and start their first copies

questions.q: Has every workload been given a recovery point and a recovery time, agreed with the business?
questions.why: Without objectives, nothing can be checked or prioritised.
questions.need: Every workload has a recovery point and time agreed with the business
questions.how: Classify workloads in tiers with the business owners

questions.q: Could an administrator account delete your backups today?
questions.need: No administrator account can delete the backups
questions.how: Keep an immutable copy that admins cannot remove

questions.q: Does the recovery plan include the network: addresses, DNS, firewall rules?
questions.why: Most failed recoveries fail on the network, not on the data.
questions.need: The recovery plan includes the network
questions.how: Add addresses, DNS and firewall changes to the plan, and test them

questions.q: Who can start a failover, and do they have the runbook at night?
questions.why: Recovery depends on people as much as on copies.
questions.need: Whoever starts a failover has the runbook, at night too
questions.how: Name who can start it, and give them a one-click plan

questions.q: When a replication falls behind, who is told and what do they do?
questions.why: A silent missed recovery point is discovered on the worst day.
questions.need: A replication that falls behind reaches a named owner
questions.how: Alert on missed recovery points with an owner and a response

questions.q: Which workloads can lose no data at all, which can lose minutes, and which can lose hours?
questions.why: Zero, minutes and hours need different replication, distances and costs.
questions.need: Every workload sits in a recovery tier (zero, minutes, hours) with the replication that matches it
questions.how: Group workloads into recovery tiers with the business and pick the replication for each

questions.q: How far back must you be able to go, and how close together must the recovery points be?
questions.why: Keeping every point forever costs storage; keeping too few loses the point you need after ransomware went unnoticed for days.
questions.need: Retention is agreed per tier: recent recovery points close together, older ones further apart
questions.how: Agree a retention scheme, for example hourly for a day, daily for a week, weekly for a month

questions.q: Which machines must come back together, in the same state and in a set order: an application with its database, say?
questions.why: Recovering machines one by one, from different moments, breaks applications that depend on each other.
questions.need: Applications that depend on each other are protected as a group and recovered in a set order
questions.how: Group dependent machines, snapshot each group together, and write the power-on order into the plan
